brief: The town's calendar, in full: a MARKET in the lane every 4th day (isMarketDay), a CONCERT on the far-bank bandstand in summer (isBandDay, bandChance = clamp((warmth - 0.42) / 0.4, 0, 1) * 0.86), a BONFIRE on the cross street 1.79 times a year (#185 counted it), and a CART down the cross street on 80% of mornings (CART_P 0.8). Grep for a plaza equivalent: there is none. The plaza is the town's civic room — a fountain that reads the year, the wind and the frost, a roundel, PLAZA_PITS, six benches, six FOUNT_STANDS, a quay rail, five bollards, a barge berth and a fourteen-place door that has refused 0 of 92 offers EVER (#183) — and in 190 iterations nothing has ever brought the town TO it. Give the plaza a recurring day of its own, on the calendar like the others, that pulls people out of the other quarters and fills it.
successLooksLike: Presence on the plaza on the day it falls, 6 seeds x a year, is a clear multiple of an ordinary day's — measured as PRESENCE, not a per-instant crop — and you can show WHERE the people came from: count the lane and courtyard bands on the same days and show they thinned, or show the event has its own source and the neighbours are flat. On every other day the plaza is unchanged.
avoid: The DOOR is not the bound — it refuses 0.0%, so capacity work here is wasted. The bound is demand, which makes this a source-and-schedule problem. A spawn BAND is a share of a budget, not a rate, so an event squeezed into an existing roll takes its crowd out of whatever sits above it in the same ladder (that is exactly what #172's allotment rung did to the plaza's own offers, 35 -> 20): if it needs its own source, give it one, and price the neighbour either way. Key the day on a salted hash(day, k) like isBandDay, never on R(). And do not make it a second market — the lane owns that.
